newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 24.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 24.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Brand-name Products, Media and the Internet
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

DUESSELDORF - Traditional advertising in Germany will grow by three to five percent in 1997, says the finance magazine "Wirtschaftswoche" based on a poll of advertising executives. Those questioned predict non-traditional advertising, including direct marketing and sponsoring, to experience a boost of three percent this year. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Media distribution income is likely to shrink in the near future due to the free access to information available on the Internet, say experts at the Frankfurt Marketing Services Fair. Print media representatives, however, say their publications will have a role in the distribution of information and opinions for years to come. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Magazines and beer companies were the biggest sponsors of television broadcasts in 1996, says the Media Control research institute. Of the 16,800 sponsored programmes, almost 3,000 were sponsored by magazines and 2,800 by beer companies, says the institute. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - James Bond, Britain's famous screen secret agent, this week picked up the keys to his new company car - a $100,000 top-of-the-line BMW 750i saloon that he will drive in a new film "Tomorrow Never Dies", slated for release in December. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Advertising agency Springer & Jacoby has won the account to introduce the new M-Class off-roader from Mercedes-Benz. The agency also recently won the accounts of Wasa crackers, Ovomaltine beverages and Isostar sport drinks.
(Horizont)

BONN - The Rhineland-Palatinate premier Kurt Beck has called on the cigarette industry to exercise greater regulation over its advertising. The upper house of parliament on Friday will deliberate on a recommendation by the public health board for a cigarette advertising ban. (Die Welt)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

HAMBURG - The tabloids "Bild" and "Bild am Sonntag" said they had 11.26 million readers last year, making them the most popular newspapers in Germany, their publisher Axel Springer Verlag AG says. (Reuter)

BADEN-BADEN - Public broadcaster ARD plans to open a capital city studio in Berlin on May 22, 1999, says ARD chairman Udo Reiter. The opening is scheduled one day before the German presidential election. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

DUESSELDORF - Specialty retailer Douglas says its net income rose two percent in 1996 to 105.6 million marks ($61.5 million), but says it expects 1997 to be a difficult year in general for retailers. However, the company says it plans to strengthen its leadership in the retail perfume market. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Publisher Langenschiedt KG says it has taken over the Bertlesmann British distribution unit GeoCenter International Ltd. GeoCenter specialises in travel, dictionaries and maps, Langenschiedt says. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - Karin Klossek will soon join Commerzbank as director of marketing for private customers as successor to Patrick W. Diemer. She is currently in the same position at BfG Bank in Frankfurt. (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Thomas Gross will soon become administration director at DeutschlandRadio. Gross is currently head of the press and public relations department of the Federal Union of German Employers Associations and a member of the television board of public broadcaster ZDF. (Frankfurter Rundschau)
